result.scientific_strategy:
## 10469e2d-31ee-4afe-a37b-5a24da0d14bb / Scientific strategy

**Direction:** The tested capacity, radial-coverage, IK branch-feasibility, target-observation, zero-entropy, checkpoint-selection, reduced-update, parallel-rollout-diversity, long-range reach-shaping, generic temporal action-smoothing, target-conditioned Jacobian action-guidance, and joint-velocity reward-regularization interventions are resolved and rejected for this transferred recipe. Experiment 10 rejected near-baseline reproduction from fresh initialization, while experiment 11 shows that a transferred PPO run with n_steps 2048 can recover a robust endpoint but not a uniformly stable trajectory. Experiments 12 and 14 show that changing entropy or reducing PPO optimization epochs does not prevent the late regression, experiment 13 shows that dense checkpointing does not expose a stable high-performing interval, experiment 15 shows that four-environment rollout diversity does not preserve endpoint quality, and experiment 16 shows that broadening the exponential closeness gradient does not change the localized negative-angle failures. Experiment 17 shows that replacing Cartesian target residuals with target polar features preserves neither the incumbent failure pattern nor full-range reliability, experiment 18 shows that generic command smoothing does not remove the incumbent failures, experiment 19 shows that a direct target-conditioned Jacobian-transpose bias leaves every incumbent failure unchanged, and experiment 20 shows that a joint-velocity penalty likewise removes none of the incumbent failures and adds new failures. Experiment 21 now tests whether reducing static motor-command authority can alter reach-side overshoot without the temporal state introduced by smoothing; it retains an explicit no-broadening criterion before the investigation shifts to seed robustness.

**Lessons and limits:** The baseline checkpoint-100352 achieved 97.75% pooled research success across two matched panels, with nine failures concentrated around -121 to -150 degrees, establishing a concrete robustness gap (`research/brief.md`; `research/evaluations/10469e2d-31ee-4afe-a37b-5a24da0d14bb`). Experiment 11 changed only PPO n_steps from 1024 to 2048 and reached 0.99 training success at 36,864 before drifting to 0.96 at 120,832, with reward falling from 115.141 to 110.994 (`research/training_logs/10469e2d-31ee-4afe-a37b-5a24da0d14bb/experiment-11-attempt-1.log`; `research/brief.md`). Its endpoint scored 98.0% on both panels and remains the strongest compatible development model. Experiments 12 and 14 retained the late training decline despite changing PPO update behavior. Experiment 15 reached a training-success peak near 0.99 and reward 118.147, but the comparable 36,864-step checkpoint scored 97.5% and 98.0%, while the 120,832-step endpoint fell to 92.0% and 91.5%. Endpoint failures included many targets outside the established negative-angle sector and repeated hold interruptions, so four environments neither suppressed drift nor preserved the localized failure pattern (`research/training_logs/10469e2d-31ee-4afe-a37b-5a24da0d14bb/experiment-15-attempt-1.log`; `research/evaluations/10469e2d-31ee-4afe-a37b-5a24da0d14bb`). In experiment 16, increasing CLOSENESS_LENGTH_SCALE from 0.05 to 0.08 produced a training peak of 1.00 at 32,768 steps but ended at 0.95 with reward falling from 116 to 104 by 120,832 (`research/training_logs/10469e2d-31ee-4afe-a37b-5a24da0d14bb/experiment-16-attempt-1.log`). Both measured checkpoints scored 97.5% on seed 2000 and 98.0% on seed 2200; their failures were the same four or five negative-angle episode identities, with no outside-sector failures but persistent no-reach and hold-interruption failures (`research/evaluations/10469e2d-31ee-4afe-a37b-5a24da0d14bb`). Experiment 17's polar observation candidate scored 84.5%/88.0% at 100,352 steps and 95.5%/93.5% at 120,832, while its endpoint retained all incumbent negative-sector failure identities, added four more negative-sector failures on each panel, and added five outside-sector failures on seed 2200 with repeated hold interruptions (`research/training_logs/10469e2d-31ee-4afe-a37b-5a24da0d14bb/experiment-17-attempt-1.log`; `research/evaluations/10469e2d-31ee-4afe-a37b-5a24da0d14bb`). Experiment 18 reached 0.99 training success at 100,352 steps and declined to 0.95 at 120,832 while reward fell from 111.53 to 102.939 (`research/training_logs/10469e2d-31ee-4afe-a37b-5a24da0d14bb/experiment-18-attempt-1.log`; `research/brief.md`). Its 100,352-step candidate scored 97.0% and 98.0%, and its endpoint scored 97.5% on both panels. At the endpoint it retained all four incumbent failure identities on each panel and added one new failed episode on each, so smoothing did not improve the localized gap and slightly reduced matched-panel reliability. Experiment 19 reached a training peak of 1.00 at 32,768 steps with reward 118.0, then declined to 0.96 and reward 102.544 at 120,832 (`research/training_logs/10469e2d-31ee-4afe-a37b-5a24da0d14bb/experiment-19-attempt-1.log`; `research/brief.md`). Its 100,352 and 120,832 checkpoints each scored 98.0% on both matched panels; each retained exactly episodes 19, 76, 112, and 188 on seed 2000 and 53, 86, 99, and 138 on seed 2200, with all failures truncated at 500 steps and no new failures outside that set (`research/evaluations/10469e2d-31ee-4afe-a37b-5a24da0d14bb`). Experiment 20 peaked at 0.99 training success at 30,720 steps and fell to 0.95 at 120,832, with reward falling from 100.692 to 95.1862 (`research/brief.md`). Its 100,352-step candidate scored 95.0% and 96.0%, and its endpoint scored 96.0% on both matched panels. At both checkpoints, every incumbent failure identity remained on each panel; the peak added six and four failures and the endpoint added four and four. Every listed failure truncated at 500 steps. Thus the velocity penalty produced no selective repair and materially weakened development reliability. The evaluations do not isolate physical failure mode from stochastic realization, but they are sufficient to reject this recipe and retain experiment 11. Development evidence remains insufficient to declare the official objective reached.

**Open questions:** The radial-coverage, tested geometry-feature, long-range reward-credit, polar target-observation, generic temporal-smoothing, target-conditioned action-guidance, and velocity-regularization distinctions are resolved for this transferred recipe. The replication question is resolved enough to change direction: experiments 3 and 10 both produced broad fresh-run failure, while experiments 1 and 11 provide robust transferred realizations. Experiments 13-15 resolve checkpoint selection, reduced update count, and four-environment rollout diversity as sufficient explanations for the strong endpoint or late regression. Experiments 19 and 20 show that deterministic target-conditioned action guidance and a velocity-aware reward do not selectively repair the recurring failures; experiment 20's added failures also show that velocity regularization can trade away full-range reliability. It remains unknown whether the persistent failures arise from physical overshoot, an unmodeled geometric branch, or stochastic policy realization. That distinction no longer affects the experiment-20 lineage decision, but it determines whether a future effort should prioritize a control-dynamics change or seed-robustness evidence.

**Conditional next steps:** Retain experiment 11 checkpoint-120832 as the working and best-known development model and restore its complete scientific recipe before the next experiment. Do not repeat the velocity penalty or the already rejected intervention families. If static action scaling removes an incumbent reach failure while keeping at least 98.0% on both matched panels and adding no outside-sector failures, pursue that control-dynamics family; if it preserves the same identities, falls below threshold, or broadens failures, run a matched transfer replication with a distinct seed to prioritize stochastic-process investigation before another behavior-preserving intervention. Do not request the terminal benchmark while either useful direction remains.
